templates.SMALL: The underwater sound of a small vessel, with a compact high-revving engine, heard as a light high-pitched engine whine.
templates.MEDIUM: The underwater sound of a medium vessel, with a medium-speed diesel engine, heard as a regular medium-tone rhythm.
templates.LARGE: The underwater sound of a large vessel, with a large slow-speed diesel engine, heard as a heavy low-frequency rumble.
templates.BG: The underwater sound of a bg vessel, with no ship nearby, heard as quiet sea.

SMALL: An outboard motor at full throttle, a thin electric whine cutting through the water.
A small fast diesel clattering away, each beat light and quick like tapping fingers.
A small propeller churning hard, a fizzy curtain of cavitation bubbles trailing aft.
All of the sound sits high in the band, treble energy with almost nothing below.
The engine beats come fast and close, a hurried rhythm with no patience in it.
A small boat accelerating away, its whine rising through the gears and fading into distance.
The sound of a harbour launch ferrying lines between ship and shore.
Nothing in this sound is heavy; where a ship would thump, this merely taps.
A small petrol engine screaming at high revolutions, its note sharp and dry.
The rattle of a compact marine diesel, brisk and mechanical, with no weight in it.
The wash of a small boat's propeller, water slapped quickly into foam and hiss.
A thin bright spectrum, the tonal energy crowded into the upper frequencies.
A quick regular pulse, firing so often the intervals nearly vanish.
The sound of a small craft passing close, arriving quickly, peaking, and gone.
A pilot boat waiting on station, its engine a quick impatient hum.
The voice is light against the sea, a thread where large vessels are ropes.
The buzz of a small outboard, nasal and insistent, like a large insect trapped under the surface.
A small diesel running quick, its firing rate high enough to blur into a coarse hum.
Cavitation crackle from a fast little screw, like static poured into the sea.
The noise of a small craft has no floor to it, no low foundation under the tone.
The rhythm of small machinery, light beats landing in a rapid even row.
Throttle changes painted in pitch, the engine leaping up and settling with each move.
The small bright voice of a rigid inflatable making way across the anchorage.
Beside the dark hum of big ships, this noise is a bright scratch on the surface.
A two-stroke engine at speed, its firing so quick the separate beats merge into a steady shriek.
Light diesel chatter from a workboat, industrious but shallow in the water.
A small propeller's bite, rapid splashing thrust heard as bright water noise.
High-frequency dominated noise, a band of brightness with the bass end missing.
Firing beats crowd together at high rate, a nervous drumming under the water.
A small boat manoeuvring nearby, bursts of high revs between moments of idle.
A fishing skiff heading out at first light, its outboard whine the only voice on the water.
The sound never touches the deep registers that heavy shipping owns.
A high-revving marine petrol engine, the sound tight, metallic and thin.
A small vessel's diesel at working speed, a dry rattling pulse high in the band.
The hiss of disturbed water behind a small hull, fizzy and short-lived.
The signature of a small vessel is written entirely in the upper registers.
A fast fluttering pulse, the tempo of an engine that never learned to slow down.
The whine swells and shrinks as the small craft circles, hunting its line.
The sound of a small patrol craft sweeping the bay in efficient passes.
Small where ships are vast, quick where they are slow, high where they are low.
MEDIUM: A medium marine diesel running steadily, its working hum balanced across the band.
The tonal energy sits in the middle of the band, between the small craft's height and the big ship's depth.
The firing beats arrive at a moderate pace, evenly spaced like a steady walk.
The sound of a coastal trawler making its grounds, machinery steady and practised.
The main engine's drone underwritten by a generator's light running hum.
The engine works under fair load, its tone firm without a trace of strain.
A medium vessel holding a steady course, its engine note a level line in the water.
Not the bright needle of the small craft, nor the deep bell of the ship, but the plain voice between.
The honest voice of a mid-sized engine, neither hurried nor laboured.
A balanced spectrum, neither top-heavy nor bottom-deep, energy spread evenly through the middle.
A sober working rhythm, each stroke landing with fair weight and fair pause.
A short-sea ferry's voice, the reliable drone of a vessel on a fixed run.
Auxiliary machinery threading through the tone, pumps and generators at their modest work.
A comfortable burden, the sound of machinery well matched to its task.
The sound arrives slowly, holds, and departs at the pace of middle tonnage.
The sound holds the middle ground, lacking the skiff's height and the liner's depth.
A six-cylinder diesel at working speed, its beats even and comfortably spaced.
The pitch is moderate, the sound occupying the centre of the water's audible range.
The pulse is measured, faster than a giant's, slower than a skiff's frantic tick.
The working hum of a harbour tug in easy transit, potent machinery at rest.
A blend of main engine and deck machinery, the layered sound of a working mid-sized hull.
The note thickens slightly with work but never labours, effort evenly carried.
Approaching the harbour with revs easing in stages, the drone stepping down.
Easier to feel than a small boat, easier to miss than a large one.
The moderate thrum of a medium vessel's machinery, steady as a heartbeat.
Mid-band frequencies carry the signature, a comfortable voice neither shrill nor cavernous.
Combustion beats in comfortable rows, the tempo of routine work.
A mid-sized cargo vessel coasting between ports, its engine even and uncomplaining.
The clean drone of the main engine with a faint auxiliary shimmer above it.
Under way and loaded, the engine's hum gains body without losing composure.
On passage at constant speed, the tone so level it becomes part of the sea.
The middle size is audible as moderation, nothing extreme in any direction.
A mid-range diesel at cruise, its tone full without being heavy.
The spectrum is full-bodied in the middle, thinning at both extremes.
A steady middling pulse, the rhythm of an engine that will run all day.
The sound of a fishing vessel of middle size, winches quiet, main engine steady.
Deck winches idle, the hydraulic whir faint against the diesel's steady stroke.
The sound of a vessel carrying its cargo without complaint.
A mid-sized craft crossing the bay, its sound widening then fading over minutes.
Between the fleet's two voices this one stands level, the tenor among sopranos and basses.
LARGE: A slow-speed diesel turning over in a vast hull, each combustion stroke a soft heavy thump.
The tonal energy lies deep in the low frequencies, a dark foundation under the sea's surface noise.
The strokes arrive with long deliberate intervals, each one a completed event.
The sound of a deeply laden hull, weight you can hear pressing the water aside.
The sound of a container ship at sea, city-sized machinery crossing the night.
The rumble arrives long before the ship, carried through water further than sight.
A monumental evenness, the same deep tone held for minutes without change.
Where the small craft writes in pencil, this voice writes in dark ink.
The deep unhurried beat of a main engine built for tonnage, not time.
Almost everything in the sound happens below where small craft live, in the bass of the water.
A slow colossal pulse, the rhythm of machinery measured in seconds rather than fractions.
Tonnage made audible, a noise with the density of cargo.
A bulk carrier's deep passage, ore and engine in one low voice.
A low voice that travels, the sound of the hull reaching the shore ahead of its wake.
The steadiness of heavy machinery, a note that does not know hurry exists.
Beside this depth the small boat's whine is a faint scribble on the surface.
A large two-stroke diesel at working revolutions, its strokes landing like distant hammers wrapped in cloth.
A deep spectrum with strong low harmonics stacked like the floors of a tower.
Beats spaced like a funeral drum, unhurried, inevitable, immense.
The loaded depth of a big ship's voice, ballast and burden in the tone.
The monotone thunder of a laden tanker crawling up the coast.
The noise fills the water for miles around, a vast slow acoustic weather.
Level as the horizon, the big ship's voice holds its single low line.
The difference is elemental, light machinery above, mass machinery below.
The monumental heartbeat of a big ship's engine room, felt in the water before it is heard.
The dominant energy sits in the sub-bass, a rumble more structural than audible.
The firing intervals stretch out, each stroke standing alone in the water.
A heavily burdened vessel, its sound as weighted as its waterline.
A big freighter's engine heard through a hull of water, the trade routes made audible.
Deep sound with long wavelengths, arriving at the ear as a presence rather than a point.
A monotone of depth, the sound of an engine that will hold this note for days.
This sound owns the bottom of the water; the small fleet only rents the top.
A slow-speed diesel's fundamental, a pulse so low and long it becomes a presence.
The sound's mass is concentrated low, the acoustic shadow cast by a huge hull.
A rhythm slow enough to count on the fingers, each beat a soft detonation of mass.
The mass of the hull lives in the noise, a richness no light craft can counterfeit.
The voice of a passenger liner at distance, steady as its schedule.
The rumble of the big ship is felt in the hull before it is heard in the air.
The great drum of the engine room keeps one beat, hour into hour.
A tone that makes middle vessels sound brief and small ones sound accidental.
BG: A calm sea at rest, the underwater world quiet beneath a still surface.
Wind fuzz on the surface, a faint spray of noise carried down through the water.
Scattered bubble clouds drifting through, each bubble a faint tick as it passes.
Distant breakers on a far shore, arriving as a muffled eternal whisper.
Tidal current moving the whole water body, a smooth laminar hush.
Light rain on the surface, each drop a soft tick transmitted down.
Near silence, the underwater world at rest, nothing mechanical anywhere.
The faint eternal background of the open ocean, always there, never insistent.
Gentle swell rolling past, heard as a slow soft breathing in the water.
Light wind combing the surface, its fizz arriving below as a soft static.
The soft pop of single bubbles somewhere above, sparse and unhurried.
The long wash of remote surf, a sound like the sea slowly turning over.
The long pull of the tide, heard as a steady drift of sound.
Rainfall drumming faintly above, arriving underwater as a fine even sizzle.
The deep quiet of open water, a stillness the ear slowly learns to hear.
A soft ambient wash, the sea's own noise floor, quiet and unbroken.
The open sea in quiet mood, its noise a soft continuous wash.
The fizz of small breaking wavelets, bubbles ticking down through the quiet.
A cloud of fine bubbles dissolving, a gentle fizz that thins to nothing.
Far-off waves on some unseen coast, their arrival a soft grey noise.
Water in slow transit, its flow a continuous soft carpet of noise.
A shower passing over calm water, its sound a gentle static from the sky.
An empty soundscape, no engines, no waves of note, only the sea's faint pulse.
The baseline hum of ocean water, beneath which nothing goes.
Low swell from a distant storm, arriving as a patient rock of the water.
A freshening breeze writing white noise across the top of the sea.
Isolated bubble clicks in the open water, the sea's smallest events.
The rumour of a distant beach, carried across miles of quiet water.
Current shearing past moorings far away, a faint rope-buzz in the distance.
Rain mixing into the surface layer, bubbles ticking as they form.
The hush between weathers, the sea holding its breath.
Ambient sea noise at its gentlest, a grey velvet quiet.
A glassy surface above and a hush below, the sea making almost no sound.
Surface agitation from wind, heard beneath as a delicate continuous hiss.
Bubbles from some distant disturbance, arriving attenuated and patient.
Remote surf heard as one continuous sigh, neither rising nor falling.
The deep drift of a flood tide, the sea moving house quietly.
The patter of drops on a still sea, the quietest percussion there is.
Acoustic stillness, the rare condition of water with nothing to say.
The ocean's resting voice, heard when nothing else claims the water.
